'''Ronny Turiaf''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|r|oʊ|n|i|_|ˈ|t|ɝː|i|ɑː|f}} {{respell|ROH|nee|_|TUR|ee|ahf}},{{citation needed|date=September 2022}} {{IPA|fr|ʁɔni tyʁijaf|lang}}; born 13 January 1983) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player who played 10 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Turiaf grew up in France and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] in the United States, where he led the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) in scoring in his senior year. After graduating from Gonzaga, he entered the [[2005 NBA draft]] and was picked by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He later played for the [[Golden State Warriors]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Miami Heat]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Turiaf won an [[NBA championship]] with Miami in 2012. He was also a member of the [[France national basketball team|French national team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ffbb.com/ronny-turiaf-officialise-sa-retraite-des-parquets|title=Ronny Turiaf officialise sa retraite des parquets|website=FFBB|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> He was inducted into the [[French Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ffbb.com/patrimoine/7-nouveaux-academiciens-du-basket-francais-0|title=7 nouveaux académiciens du basket français|access-date=January 21, 2024}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Born in [[Fort-de-France]],<ref>{{Cite journal|date=September 2018|title=Moi, je... Ronny Turiaf|journal=Basket (Les Éditions Atao)|volume=22|pages=54}}</ref> Turiaf spent most of his childhood in [[Martinique]], a French [[Overseas departments and regions of France|overseas departments]] in the [[Caribbean Sea]]. Following the advice from his father, Turiaf moved to [[Paris]] in 1998, at the age of 15, to attend the National Institute of Physical Education ([[INSEP]]), a school that combines rigorous secondary education with elite-level athletic training.<ref name="nbabio" />

In 1999, he made the [[France national under-18 basketball team|French Under-18 national team]], and he helped lead the team to the gold medal at the [[2000 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] with future NBA stars [[Tony Parker]], [[Boris Diaw]], and [[Mickaël Piétrus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/071124_ronnyturiaf_warrior.html|title=RONNY TURIAF: A Multicultural Warrior|website=[[NBA.com]] |year=2007|access-date=March 27, 2008}}</ref>

== College career ==
In 2001, Turiaf left France after accepting an offer to attend [[Gonzaga University]] in [[Spokane, Washington]], where he played for four years. In his last three years at Gonzaga, he was named First Team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]].<ref name="nbabio" /> Additionally, in his senior year (2004–05), he was named the conference's Player of the Year.<ref name="nbabio" /> He ended his college career as the fourth all-time leader in scoring and rebounding in school history, with 1,723 points and 859 rebounds, respectively.<ref name="nbabio" /> He averaged 13.6 points and 6.8 rebounds per game through his college years at Gonzaga, but led the WCC averaging 15.9 points, 9.5 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game as a senior.<ref name="nbabio" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/roster/0607_21turiaf.html|title=#21 Ronny Turiaf|website=[[NBA.com]] |year=2007|access-date=March 27, 2008}}</ref> He graduated from Gonzaga with a degree in sports management, communication and French. He was the first triple major in his family.<ref name="nbabio" />

== Professional career ==

=== Los Angeles Lakers ===

==== 2005–06 season ====
[[File:Ronny-Turiaf 03-23-08 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Turiaf in the Los Angeles Lakers uniform. He played for Lakers from 2006 to 2008.]]
Ronny Turiaf was the 37th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], signing a two-year, $1 million contract. After a physical exam conducted by the Lakers just four weeks after the draft, team doctor, John Moe, found an enlarged [[aortic root]] in Turiaf's heart. After multiple examinations by other physicians, the Lakers decided that the problem, which was cleared by doctors in both France and the NBA's pre-Draft camp, was serious enough to require surgery. The Lakers were forced to void Turiaf's contract but retained his rights in case he was cleared to play again after the surgery. In addition, the team paid for all the expenses from the surgery. Turiaf underwent the six-hour open-heart surgery on 26 July 2005. His expected recovery time was between six and twelve months.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spokesmanreview.com/local/story.asp?ID=81378|title=Turiaf needs heart surgery|year=2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070212075227/http://www.spokesmanreview.com/local/story.asp?ID%3D81378|archive-date=February 12, 2007|url-status=dead|access-date=March 27, 2008}}</ref>

As part of his rehabilitation, Turiaf signed with the [[Continental Basketball Association]]'s [[Yakama Sun Kings]], a team that drafted him with their 36th pick in the 2005 CBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/cba-draft.shtml|title=CBA Draft|year=2005|access-date=March 27, 2008}}</ref> He played nine games with the Sun Kings, averaging 13 points and 6.3 rebounds per game. Turiaf recovered from his surgery quicker than expected and was therefore re-signed with the Lakers on 17 January 2006, less than six months after his surgery. In order to make room on the team's 15-man roster, the Lakers waived guard [[Laron Profit]] after his season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2296001|title=Six months after heart surgery, Turiaf joins Lakers|year=2006|access-date=March 27, 2008}}</ref>

==== 2006–07 season ====
On 1 November 2006, in the second game of the season, Ronny Turiaf scored career highs in almost every category against the [[Golden State Warriors]], including 8/10 shooting with 23 points and 14 rebounds.

==== 2007–08 season ====
Turiaf received playing time due to the many Laker injuries during the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]]. He was in the starting line-up at the beginning of the season as a forward alongside [[Lamar Odom]], but after spraining his left ankle during practice on 15 November 2007, Turiaf missed two games of his own while his starts became limited.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://my.lakers.com/blogs/2007/11/15/turiaf-injured-in-practice/|title=Turiaf Injured in Practice|year=2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080505040355/http://my.lakers.com/blogs/2007/11/15/turiaf-injured-in-practice/|archive-date=May 5, 2008|url-status=dead|access-date=March 30, 2008}}</ref> However, after [[Pau Gasol]] sprained his ankle on 14 March 2008 in [[New Orleans Hornets|New Orleans]], Ronny took over as the starting center for nine games until Gasol returned on April 2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://my.lakers.com/blogs/2008/03/14/pau-ankle-injury/|title=Pau Ankle Injury|year=2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080412101243/http://my.lakers.com/blogs/2008/03/14/pau-ankle-injury/|archive-date=April 12, 2008|url-status=dead|access-date=March 30, 2008}}</ref> In that nine game span, Turiaf's stats jumped to over 30 minutes per game with 11 points, 6 rebounds, and 2 blocks. Yet the Lakers went 5–4 during those nine games, including back-to-back losses at home against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] and the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], two of the league's worst teams. Turiaf and the Lakers would reach the [[2008 NBA Finals]], but they would lose in six games to their arch rivals [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20080328/MEMLAL/recap.html|title=Bryant Scores Just Six of His 53 in Final Quarter|website=[[NBA.com]] |year=2008|access-date=April 13, 2008}}</ref>

During his time with the Lakers, Turiaf developed a close friendship with teammate [[Kobe Bryant]]. Bryant expressed sadness upon Turiaf's departure from the Lakers<ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.pn/2bJ03O9|title=Kobe Bryant: Sad to See Ronny Turiaf Go|year=2008|access-date=February 11, 2020}}</ref> and would later say that Turiaf was one of his four all-time favorite teammates.
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slamonline.com/archives/kobe-bryant-names-his-four-closest-teammates-of-his-career/|title=Kobe Bryant Names His Four Closest Teammates of His Career|year=2016|access-date=February 11, 2020}}</ref>

=== Golden State Warriors ===
On 9 July 2008, Ronny Turiaf agreed to a four-year, $17 million contract offer from the Golden State Warriors. According to [[Free agent|free agency]] rules, his previous team, the Los Angeles Lakers, had seven days to match that offer.

The Lakers, on July 18, decided not to match the Warriors' offer and the deal was finalized.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_ronny_turiaf.html|title=Warriors Signing Of Free Agent Ronny Turiaf Finalized|website=[[NBA.com]] |year=2008|access-date=July 19, 2008}}</ref>

=== New York Knicks ===
[[File:Ronny Turiaf Knicks 2010.jpg|thumb|Turiaf with the New York Knicks in 2010]]
On 9 July 2010 Turiaf was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] along with [[Anthony Randolph]], [[Kelenna Azubuike]] and a future second-round pick in a [[sign and trade]] deal for [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/randolph_acquired070910.html|title=Knicks Acquire Randolph, Azubuike & Turiaf|date=July 9, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=July 9, 2010}}</ref>

=== ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne ===
During the [[2011 NBA lockout]] he signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne]] in his native France.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/31828/asvel_officially_announces_ronny_turiaf.html|title=ASVEL, ufficiale la firma di Ronny Turiaf|work=Sportando|access-date=November 19, 2017|language=en}}</ref>

=== Washington Wizards ===
On 10 December 2011, Turiaf was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards_acquire_turiaf_121011.html|title=WIZARDS ACQUIRE TURIAF|date=December 10, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref>

=== Miami Heat ===
On 15 March 2012, Turiaf was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] along with [[JaVale McGee]] in a three-way trade involving the [[Denver Nuggets]], the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/mcgee_trade_03_15_2012.html|title=Nuggets acquire McGee, Turiaf, draft pick from Washington|date=March 15, 2012|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=March 16, 2012}}</ref> He was waived by the Nuggets shortly afterwards.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/nuggets-waive-turiaf/|title=Nuggets waive Turiaf|date=March 18, 2012|work=Fox News|access-date=November 19, 2017|language=en-US}}</ref>

On 21 March 2012, Turiaf signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_signs_ronny_turiaf_2012_03_21.html | title=Heat Signs Ronny Turiaf | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc | date=March 21, 2012 | access-date=March 21, 2012}}</ref> On 21 June 2012 Turiaf won his first NBA championship.

=== Los Angeles Clippers ===
On 27 July 2012, Turiaf signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-free-agent-ronny-turiaf|title=CLIPPERS SIGN FREE AGENT RONNY TURIAF|date=July 27, 2012|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref> Turiaf made 65 appearances for Los Angeles during the [[2012–13 NBA season]], recording averages of 1.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ronny Turiaf 2012-13 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2789/type/nba/year/2013|access-date=August 18, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== Minnesota Timberwolves ===
On 18 July 2013, Turiaf signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/18/wolves-sign-big-man-turiaf.ap/|title=Wolves sign free-agent center Turiaf to two-year deal|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 19, 2017|language=en-US}}</ref> He managed 31 games for Minnesota in 2013–14, but only two games in 2014–15 after being ruled out for the rest of the season on 16 December 2014, after undergoing a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right hip.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/ronny-turiaf-injury-update-0|title=Ronny Turiaf Injury Update {{!}} Minnesota Timberwolves|work=Minnesota Timberwolves|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref> Three days later, he was acquired by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a three-team trade that involved the Timberwolves and the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141219-trade|title=Sixers Acquire 2015 Second-round Pick, Ronny Turiaf, And Rights To Sergei Lishouk {{!}} Philadelphia 76ers|work=Philadelphia 76ers|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the 76ers on 23 December 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141223-thomas-signed|title=Sixers Sign Free Agent Malcolm Thomas {{!}} Philadelphia 76ers|work=Philadelphia 76ers|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref>

Turiaf announced his retirement from basketball on 24 October 2016,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Ronny-turiaf-met-un-terme-a-sa-carriere-sportive/739940|title=Ronny Turiaf met un terme à sa carrière sportive|newspaper=L'Equipe.fr|language=fr-FR|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> almost two years after having appeared in his last game and after having been plagued by hip pain for a long time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-france/ronny-turiaf-raccroche.html|title=Ronny Turiaf raccroche|website=BeBasket|access-date=October 24, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024113439/http://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-france/ronny-turiaf-raccroche.html|archive-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref>

== National team career ==
[[File:France Olympic basketball players disappointed, Sergio Llull excited.jpg|thumb|Turiaf (far left) with the French national team in 2012]]
Turiaf represented the senior [[France national basketball team|French national team]] internationally. With France, he competed at the following major tournaments: the [[2003 EuroBasket]], the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/32258/sid/3507/tid/282/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_World_Championship/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919021154/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/32258/sid/3507/tid/282/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_World_Championship/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 19, 2015|title=Ronny Turiaf profile, FIBA World Championship 2006|newspaper=FIBA.COM|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> the [[2007 EuroBasket]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2007.roundID_3972.teamID_282.playerID_32258.html|title=Ronny Turiaf {{!}} EuroBasket (2007) {{!}} FIBA Europe|website=www.fibaeurope.com|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> the [[2009 EuroBasket]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.roundID_6328.season_2009.teamID_282.playerID_32258.html|title=Ronny Turiaf {{!}} EuroBasket (2009) {{!}} FIBA Europe|website=www.fibaeurope.com|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> and the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 London Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.olympic.org/ronny-turiaf|title=Ronny TURIAF – Olympic Basketball {{!}} France|date=June 26, 2016|newspaper=International Olympic Committee|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Turiaf can speak five languages: French, English, Spanish, Italian, and [[Antillean Creole]] (his native language).<ref name="nbabio">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ronny_turiaf/bio.html|title=Ronny Turiaf Bio Page|website=[[NBA.com]] |year=2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060918142703/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ronny_turiaf/bio.html|archive-date=September 18, 2006|url-status=dead|access-date=March 24, 2008}}</ref> He has four younger sisters: Elodie, Florence, Nadia, and Rachelle.<ref name="nbabio" />

In August 2009, Turiaf set up his "Heart to Heart" Foundation to provide medical care to children who do not have health insurance and cannot afford the care they need. According to the Foundation's website, the mission is "to provide support, including echocardiograms to people with heart related issues so they can live a healthy and happy life."<ref>{{cite web|title=ABOUT THE HEART TO HEART FOUNDATION|url=http://ronnyturiaf.me/?page_id=409|work=RonnyTuriaf.me|access-date=December 17, 2014}}</ref>
